chunks: Ja'far b. Muhammad narrated to us, from al-Husayn b. Muhammad, from his uncle 'Abd Allah b. 'Amir, from Sulayman b. Hafs al-Marwazi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both) saying:

Whoever visits the grave of my son Ali (peace be upon him), he shall have seventy accepted Hajj with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. I said: Seventy accepted Hajj? He said: Yes, and seventy thousand Hajj. I said: Seventy thousand accepted Hajj? He said: Then he said: Many a Hajj is not accepted. Whoever visits him or stays overnight at his shrine, it shall be like one who visited Allah at His Throne. I said: Like one who visited Allah at His Throne? He said: Yes. When it is the Day of Resurrection, there shall be upon the Throne of Allah, Exalted is His Majesty, four from the ancients and four from the later ones. The ancients: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa. The four later ones: Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn. Then the carpet shall be extended, and the visitors of the Imams' graves shall sit with us — except that the highest in rank and closest in privilege shall be the visitors of the grave of my son Ali (peace be upon him).

The Shaykh, the jurist Abu Ja'far (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The meaning of his saying (peace be upon him) 'shall be like one who visited Allah at His Throne' is not a likening, because the angels visit the Throne, seek refuge in it, circumambulate around it, and say: 'We visit Allah at His Throne,' just as people say: 'We make pilgrimage to the House of Allah, and we visit Allah' — not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is described with a place. Exalted is He far above that greatly.

key_terms.حجة مبرورة: Accepted Hajj — a Hajj pilgrimage accepted by Allah
key_terms.زيارة: Visitation — pilgrimage to an Imam's shrine
key_terms.عرش: Throne — the divine Throne (Arsh) of Allah

ai.seo_question: What reward did Imam al-Kadhim promise for visiting Imam al-Rida's grave?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my son Ali shall have seventy accepted Hajj pilgrimages with Allah.' When the narrator expressed astonishment, the Imam escalated to seventy thousand Hajj, adding that many Hajj are not even accepted. He then stated that visiting Imam al-Rida's shrine or staying one night there is like visiting Allah at His Throne. On the Day of Resurrection, four from the ancients (Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa) and four from the later ones (Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn) will be upon Allah's Throne, and the visitors of the Imams' graves will sit with them — with the highest rank belonging to visitors of Imam al-Rida's grave. Al-Saduq then explains the 'visiting Allah at His Throne' metaphor is not literal anthropomorphism, but refers to how angels visit the Throne and people say 'we visit Allah' when performing Hajj.
